advice: Propose a fused K-block path in the full512 assembly, replacing the pack-then-compute sequence at `Llibxsmm_78` and the operand loads in `Llibxsmm_478`/`Llibxsmm_70c`. For each 32-row by 16-K slice, load a small row-major A tile, transpose it into vectors, and feed those vectors directly to the existing FP32 MOPA accumulators before moving to the next K slice. Keep the current output-column traversal, stores, general-size fallback, and one SME region. This removes writes of the full 128 KiB A scratch panel per 64-row band. It repeats A loading and transpose work for each of the 16 output-column panels: about 262,144 A elements loaded/transposed in the existing pack, versus about 4,194,304 in the fused path. The existing compute also reads about 16 MiB of packed A across those column panels; the fused path avoids those scratch reads but adds repeated source loads and transpose instructions. Whether this trades well is unverified. This differs from the prior 16-row scratch proposal, which retained scratch and packed each row once.
risks: The MOPA accumulators occupy ZA, so the transpose tile must use registers or a non-conflicting ZA arrangement; otherwise it can destroy accumulated results. Source A accesses are strided by 512 floats across rows, and repeating them 16 times may cost more than the removed scratch traffic. Exact mapping of the 32 output rows, 16 K values, B vectors, and four ZA accumulators needs a register-level design before implementation. Check pointer bounds and K order, ABI and SME state, beta-zero writes, full n=512 correctness at tolerance 0.002, general sizes and tails, n<=0, and fresh inputs with output overwrite. Then use fresh paired controls under unchanged power settings and gates. Keep the incumbent unless the fixed promotion rules pass; noisy outcomes do not establish causality or an advisor-specific effect.
